page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. The instance features 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical AMD EPYC 9T24 cores running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 32.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio with 2.0 GB per virtual core. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 vector extensions (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16), AES, VAES, and SHA_NI cryptographic acceleration. Networking capabilities include a 7 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and the configuration does not include attached local storage or dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark results reveal strong single-core performance, ranking in the top 25 percent for single-core stress-ng CPU execution and Geekbench single-core scoring. Multi-core operations, including PassMark CPU tests and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, maintain average performance tiers. A key hardware tradeoff manifests in memory subsystem behavior: while small-block cached memory bandwidth is high at 1216.18 GB/sec, large-block uncached read memory bandwidth falls into the lower 25 percent tier at 36.9 GB/sec. This compute-centric configuration provides favorable resource density for CPU-bound tasks, offering cost efficiency for workloads that rely primarily on raw processing speed and vectorized compute instructions without requiring massive RAM capacity or local NVMe storage.

Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.4xlarge is well suited for compute-bound applications, including code compilation, text processing, batch processing, static web serving, key-value caching services like Redis, and web application backend deployments.
